item.title: Binance Hack Costs $6.3 Billion, Other Cyberattacks Escalate
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: One Laptop Cost Binance $6.3 Billion, and That Wasn't Even the Scariest Hack This Week
Binance suffered a $6.3 billion crypto heist linked to North Korea, traced to a fake job interview scam targeting an employee. Hackers used malware to steal funds, which Binance plans to cover with stablecoin freezes and reserves. Meanwhile, cyberattacks escalated in Europe, with hackers spoiling supermarket food and then targeting blood plasma storage facilities. Security researchers warned against relying on AI for password generation, noting it fails to follow secure practices. A hacker used AI agents to launch 1,200 attacks on over 100 corporate sites, including Cummins and SharkNinja, spending $5,000 in tokens. A separate botnet of 1.3 million pre-backdoored Android TV boxes was discovered, used for ad fraud and illegal traffic routing. Google and authorities shut down the botnet, but similar risks remain in gray markets. Experts advise caution with untrusted hardware and password managers.

item.title: Hera probe captures first close-up of DART impact site on Didymos
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Europe’s Hera Probe Sends Back Its Closest View Yet of NASA’s DART Crash Site
The European Space Agency’s Hera probe has captured the first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system from 37 miles away. The black-and-white photo reveals the previously unseen side of Didymos, showing features like boulders, craters, and grooves that may have formed after NASA’s DART spacecraft crashed into Dimorphos in September 2022. The impact shortened Dimorphos’s orbital period around Didymos from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes. Hera, launched in October 2024, aims to study the full effects of the collision to assess DART’s potential as a planetary defense strategy. Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator, called the view ‘a whole new world.’ The spacecraft will spend at least six months analyzing the asteroid pair, with Michael Kueppers noting the team is ready to ‘systematically map all the changes’ caused by the impact. The image highlights the asteroid’s previously hidden backside, offering new insights into the aftermath of the human-induced cosmic collision.

item.title: Blue Origin delays New Glenn launch to January
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Rocket Report: Artemis II literally tore through the atmosphere; New Glenn delay
Blue Origin delayed its New Glenn rocket's return-to-flight mission from December to January 2024. The company continues rebuilding its damaged launch pad at Cape Canaveral following a catastrophic explosion six months prior. NASA, Amazon, and the Space Force expressed urgency for the rocket's resumption. Meanwhile, Argo Space, founded by the Carlisle brothers in late 2022, is testing water-based propulsion systems for satellites. Their first mission failed in July due to a solar array deployment issue, but two more tests are planned for 2027. The system uses solar power to split water into hydrogen and oxygen gases for thrust, eliminating the need for separate propellant tanks. The technology aims to reduce reliance on Earth-based propellants for space operations.

item.title: NASA Adds X-70 Fractal to Historic X-Plane Lineup
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Meet the X-70 Fractal, the Latest Jet to Join NASA’s Historic X-Plane Lineup
NASA announced the X-70 Fractal as the latest addition to its X-plane experimental aircraft program. The reusable, configurable jet is designed to test advanced flight-control systems and maneuverability in crewed flight. Laurie Grindle, director of NASA’s Aeronautics Division, stated the X-plane program has long advanced aviation technologies. The X-70 features a modular design allowing interchangeable internal and external payloads, with a capacity of 2,000 pounds. It has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds, cruises at Mach 0.75, and reaches 45,000 feet. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called it a 'high-performance platform' for testing cutting-edge technologies. The X-70 joins a lineage of experimental aircraft dating to the 1940s, including the Bell X-1 and X-15. The program aims to push aviation boundaries by safely testing risky or complex technologies in flight.

item.title: Mantle activity may explain Earth's Great Unconformity
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
Geoscientists Nicolas Flament and Santosh Dhungana propose that Earth's mantle activity created the Great Unconformity, a massive gap in the rock record visible in the Grand Canyon. The unconformity marks a missing interval between ancient crystalline rocks and Cambrian-era sandstones, spanning 200 to over 1 billion years. Their study in Nature suggests slow mantle currents uplifted continents, exposing them to glacial erosion that carved the gap. Glaciers, which are 10 times more effective than rivers at eroding rock, likely ground down continents before sediments buried the scar. Sediments on the unconformity in North America date to 635–482 million years ago, but the gap isn't global, contradicting the Snowball Earth theory. Flament notes the anomaly hints at deep mantle processes shaping Earth's surface over millions of years.

item.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools publicly exposed online
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
Security researchers found hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools publicly exposed online, allowing unauthorized access to vulnerable systems. The Chinese-made open-source tool, used for automated penetration testing, has been linked to multiple cyberattacks since its July release. Censys identified over 800 distinct Artex deployments accessible without passwords, though some are used for authorized testing. Microsoft described Artex as a system of AI agents capable of conducting attacks with minimal human input. CrowdStrike attributed attacks on South Korean financial institutions and ConnectWise to Chinese-linked hackers using Artex, which exploited weak passwords and lacked multi-factor authentication. The tools’ public exposure enabled rapid data theft from cloud environments, with attackers leveraging simple misconfigurations. Artex’s creator has transitioned to closed-source, but code remains available on code-sharing platforms. The findings highlight how open-source tools can inadvertently expose systems if misconfigured, increasing attack surfaces for malicious actors.

item.title: Google Updates Googlebooks for Better Performance and Stability
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google just made Googlebooks faster, more stable, and less crash-prone
Google released an update for Googlebooks, improving performance and stability. Key changes include optimized NPU drivers and AICore memory management, freeing 3GB to 6GB of system RAM, which benefits laptops with 16GB RAM. Chrome now recovers memory more effectively during heavy workloads, reducing crashes and tab reloads. Convertibles no longer lose input when switching between tablet and laptop modes. Zoom crashes using simulated backgrounds and filters are fixed. External displays now support DRM-protected content like Netflix. USB microphones and multichannel audio interfaces work reliably, with reduced Bluetooth audio-video sync delays. Linux users gain terminal fixes, including stable shell sessions and improved SSH port forwarding. The November 1, 2026 Android security patch resolves 60 vulnerabilities, alongside Linux 6.18 kernel and Ti50 firmware updates. The update is rolling out to Acer, ASUS, Lenovo, HP, and Dell devices via Settings > System > System Update. Users can check for build CL3B.260622.286.R2. Early feedback on Reddit is positive, though some report Chrome spell check and notification sync issues after sleep.

item.title: FAA replaces floppy disks with modern air traffic control system
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls "historic" tech upgrade
The FAA announced it will replace floppy disks in its air traffic control system with the Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS). The upgrade, part of a six-year effort, aims to modernize outdated technology used since the 1980s. E-IDS will be installed at 435 facilities, replacing systems that face technical end-of-life issues. The new system will improve distribution of weather alerts (PIREP) and Notices to Airmen (NOTAM), critical for aviation safety. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford emphasized the shift from manual processes to a modern system enabling real-time sharing of flight alerts and restricted airspace data. The first installations will occur at Atlantic City, Nashville, Rochester airports, and Atlanta/Salt Lake City hubs, with full deployment planned by 2028. Acting FAA Administrator Chris Rocheleau previously stated the move would eliminate floppy disks and paper strips. The upgrade is framed as a historic step to enhance operational efficiency and safety across the National Airspace System.

item.title: Sequoia ends Scouts program, signaling shift in venture capital strategies
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era
Sequoia announced the shutdown of its Scouts program and closure of its London office, signaling a shift in venture capital strategies. The Scouts model, pioneered by Sequoia 17 years ago, allowed select founders to write checks on the firm’s behalf. However, increased competition and scrutiny have led to questions about its effectiveness, with critics like VC Sheel Mohnot arguing it failed to prevent missed opportunities like Uber. Sequoia framed the move as a need for focus, emphasizing fewer investments. Rival firm a16z revamped its scout program, giving scouts more resources but reducing numbers. Founders benefit from scouting roles by gaining visibility and relationships. Roxanne Varza, a former Sequoia scout, lamented the closure, crediting the program for fostering Europe’s investment culture. Despite concerns, scouts may persist for early-stage and niche deals, though the model’s broader role is being reevaluated. Varza noted venture partner-style deals are likely to continue, with scouts serving as a scaled approach.

item.title: Nvidia mandates GPU tracking in Southeast Asia to curb chip smuggling
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims
Southeast Asia computing providers must now register with Nvidia's Fleet Intelligence tracking system to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners, per Bloomberg. The requirement aims to monitor AI GPU deployments amid U.S. concerns about restricted hardware reaching China via smuggling networks. Fleet Intelligence, introduced in December as a data center management tool, collects hardware location data but remains voluntary outside the NCP mandate. Nvidia has not clarified if existing partners must enroll or if the policy will expand beyond Southeast Asia. The company has developed software-based GPU tracking since December 2022, using telemetry and latency to estimate chip locations. C4ADS found $13.4 million in Nvidia GPUs moving through regional trade routes, linked to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which faces U.S. and Singaporean investigations. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended ties to Megaspeed, while its data center landlord terminated its contract. Super Micro is also under scrutiny for allegedly diverting $2.5 billion in Nvidia servers to China. Nvidia has removed half its Asian buyers and requires 51% of computing services to be outside China.

item.title: Apple Reports Over 100,000 Apps Optimized for iPhone Duo
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple
Apple reports over 100,000 apps are now optimized for the iPhone Duo, with thousands added daily. New additions include Microsoft Word, Zoom, NBA and NHL sports apps, Etsy, and productivity tools like Goodnotes. Non-optimized apps display a black bar, reducing usability. Apple hosted over 50 in-person workshops across 19 cities, attended by more than 2,000 developers. The Duo, priced at $1,999, sold out quickly, with shipping delays extending into 2024. Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Developer Relations, praised developers for embracing the device. Notable updates include Spotify, CBS, and Google Chat, though some, like Spotify, still show the black bar. Apple expects full optimizations soon. The App Store lists over 100 apps optimized for the Duo, though not all updates have rolled out yet.

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole user credentials and tokens
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis confirmed hackers accessed sensitive data, including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens, for all its users after a network breach. The attack, which occurred in October, involved AI-assisted offensive techniques allowing unauthorized access to internal tools. Affected customers include government agencies like the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the US Air Force, as well as private firms such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. Chainalysis stated that non-sensitive data like user IDs, full names, and email addresses were accessed, though it’s unclear if this exposed customers to further risks. A Wednesday update revealed an ongoing cyberattack included an on-path attack, also known as an adversary-in-the-middle attack, which exposed some customer passwords. The company identified and fixed the attack vector but has not disclosed where the infrastructure compromise occurred or if the data was TLS encrypted. The breach highlights vulnerabilities in blockchain analysis platforms handling high-profile clients.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 6 Gboard gestures most Android users never discover
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Gboard offers advanced gestures for Android users, including glide deletion to remove words instead of characters. Users can slide left on the 'Delete/Backspace' key to highlight text word-by-word for precise deletions. The spacebar functions as a horizontal trackpad by swiping left or right to move the cursor. Secondary symbols on keys can be accessed via flicking down or holding, with options like '-' on 'f' or '$' on 'd'. The floating keyboard allows resizing and repositioning for better visibility. A quick swipe up from the comma key opens Gboard settings without leaving the current app. Highlighting text and pressing Shift toggles capitalization settings. These features require Android 7.0+ and Gboard 9.0+, though some may be enabled by default on manufacturer-custom OS. Users can explore these gestures to enhance typing efficiency and reduce repetitive actions.

item.title: Razer Launches $80 Earbuds with ANC, RGB, and No Charging Needed
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Razer’s new $80 earbuds have ANC and RGB, and you don’t need to charge them
Razer has launched the Hammerhead V3 Chroma, a pair of USB-C wired earbuds priced at $79.99. The earbuds feature active noise cancellation, dual drivers for bass and treble, and customizable RGB lighting. They include THX 7.1 Surround Sound for gaming and four audio presets for different use cases. A 90-degree USB-C connector reduces cable interference during gameplay. The wired design eliminates the need for charging, though the connected device powers ANC and RGB features. Additional specs include an in-line controller, omnidirectional microphone, and IPX4 splash resistance. Available now through Razer’s store and authorized retailers, the product follows the release of the Barracuda V2 Pro.

item.title: Fox Completes $22B Roku Acquisition, Expands Media Empire
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: Fox Completes $22 Billion Acquisition of Roku, Expanding Media Empire
Fox Corporation finalized its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, completing the deal five months after its June announcement. The U.S. Department of Justice approved the transaction following antitrust review. Roku, which serves over 100 million households, will operate under Fox’s ownership, joining assets like Tubi, Fox One, and Red Seat Ventures. Roku founder Anthony Wood will co-lead Fox Digital Platforms. The acquisition follows declining Fox News ratings, with viewership down 27% year-over-year in October, while CNN and MS NOW saw gains. Lachlan Murdoch oversaw the deal, which accelerated from a 2024 projected close. The move aligns with media consolidation trends, including the Paramount-Skydance merger. Fox assures Roku will remain an open platform, though concerns persist about potential preferential treatment for Fox-owned services. The deal aims to bolster advertising, strengthen connected TV presence, and reduce reliance on traditional TV distribution. Regulatory scrutiny focuses on the combined entity’s influence over content and audience engagement.

item.title: Man survives knife through eye and brain after emergency surgery
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
A man in his 20s arrived at a UK hospital with a 15 mm knife protruding from his face, having pierced his right eye, brain, and skull. Despite the severe injury, he was conscious, talking, and moving all limbs, though agitated. Doctors scored his Glasgow Coma Scale at 12, indicating a moderate brain injury. Concerned he might attempt to remove the knife himself, they sedated and intubated him, administering antibiotics and imaging the injury. The blade had traversed the left frontal and temporal lobes, missing critical structures like the corpus callosum and internal capsule. It narrowly avoided damaging the left internal carotid artery but indented a branch of the middle cerebral artery. Surgeons opted for a 'pull-and-see' approach, removing the blade without invasive surgery. No major bleeding was found, and the brain wound was cleaned. His right eye was removed due to irreparable damage, but he remains stable. The case was reported in BMJ Case Report.

item.title: Underdog releases 32MB speech model in retro game demo
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo
Underdog released a 32MB speech model called Woof as part of a retro-themed game demo. The model runs locally on devices without internet, enabling features like typing text that is spoken back and generating music via a tuner. The game includes a typewriter, CRT monitor, and desk lamp with sound effects. Sigil Wen, founder of Underdog, emphasized building open, American-made models for privacy, allowing users to own their data. The company also launched a 167MB speech-to-text model, Bark, and a 27-billion-parameter model for laptops. Wen argued that future models could run on existing devices, offering local AI experiences. The demo highlights efforts to shift from cloud-based AI to edge devices, supporting personal assistants and personalized content creation.

item.title: OpenAI Raises $11 Billion in Funding Round Valued at $1.25 Trillion
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
OpenAI has raised $11 billion in a new funding round, valuing the AI lab at $1.25 trillion, according to Bloomberg. The round, which has not yet closed, could total up to $20 billion in the coming weeks. This falls short of the $30 billion target initially reported in late September. Bloomberg also noted potential buyers of Anthropic’s IPO are considering a lower valuation, with some estimating as low as $1.1 trillion compared to earlier expectations of $2 trillion. OpenAI previously delayed its planned IPO but remains expected to go public next year. Market uncertainty persists amid political shifts and regulatory concerns over data centers, with Democratic gains in the U.S. midterms fueling apprehension about future oversight.

item.title: Google’s Find Hub alerts users when leaving items behind with compatible trackers
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google’s Find Hub can finally warn you when you leave something behind, even if the tracker isn’t from Google
Google’s Find Hub app now alerts users when they leave items behind, even if the tracker isn’t Google-made. The 'Notify when left behind' feature pings users’ phones when they walk away from a compatible tracker, provided it’s not in a saved location. Users enable the setting per tracker via the app’s settings menu. The feature works with Moto Tag and Chipolo trackers linked to Android phones, available in the US and parts of Europe. It’s part of version 3.1.787-06. Google joins Apple and Samsung in offering similar alerts, though it’s late to the market. The update emphasizes cross-brand support, allowing non-Google trackers to work with the feature. Users are advised to enable it for critical items like wallets and keys to avoid annoyance from false alerts.

item.title: Amazon lets users text Alexa to shop, expands feature
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: You'll soon be able to text Alexa to shop on Amazon
Amazon is rolling out a new Alexa feature allowing users to text the AI for shopping tasks. The feature, available by invitation in the US, lets customers request groceries, gifts, reorders, and more via text. Alexa can also process photo attachments to find matching products, suggest items, and add them to the cart. Users can set alerts for sales, track pricing history, and check delivery status. Requests sync with the Amazon Shopping app and website. Amazon invites users to sign up via a link, requiring a phone number for access. The feature aims to streamline shopping by learning user habits for better recommendations over time.

item.title: Apple plans to remove iPhone Action button by 2027
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple might be getting rid of the iPhone’s Action button already
Apple is planning to remove the dedicated Action button from new iPhones in late 2027, according to Weibo tipster Instant Digital. The company intends to merge the button's functions with Camera Control, allowing a single press to open the camera and a long press to trigger previously assigned Action button functions. Camera Control will remain, handling photography, video recording, and adjustments. Critics note the potential for confusion with existing gestures and the challenge of repurposing long-press actions. Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra uses a similar dual-function Side button setup, though Apple's rumored implementation includes more features. The redesign is part of preparations for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary in 2027, with rumors of solid-state controls and curved glass. Apple has a history of experimenting with button designs, though not all concepts reach production. The change remains uncertain and could face design challenges.

item.title: Dawn of War 4 director picks Adeptus Mechanicus over other factions for gameplay uniqueness
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director says King Art considered adding other factions to the game like Death Guard, but decided on Adeptus Mechanicus because 'lore-wise' it's the most 'interesting in terms of gameplay'
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen revealed King Art considered adding other factions like Death Guard but chose Adeptus Mechanicus for its gameplay uniqueness. Theysen explained the team aimed to include Orks and Necrons, with Necrons deemed 'interesting' as they were promised for Dawn of War 3 but never added. After selecting Space Marines as the third faction, the remaining slot was filled by Adeptus Mechanicus, which Theysen called 'the most interesting in terms of gameplay.' He noted Death Guard's slower playstyle made it feel similar to existing factions, while AdMech's speed and ranged attacks offered a distinct experience. Theysen emphasized AdMech's lore significance as a faction never included in previous Dawn of War games, making it the 'biggest and most important' choice.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Insurers Scrutinize Crypto Security After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Insurers After $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist: D’oh!
Insurers are re-evaluating crypto security practices after a $6.3 billion hack of Binance. Industry experts warn that underwriters will scrutinize crypto firms' vulnerabilities, with Marsh’s Jacqueline Quintal noting existing policies for such losses don’t exist. Alan Lyons of Herrick said underwriters will reassess aggregate exposure and policy terms. Cyber insurance trends show fewer claims but higher payouts, with NAIC reporting average claims for large businesses rose 586% since 2021. Lloyd’s requires exclusions for state-backed attacks since 2023, and Marcos Alvarez said it’s unclear if insurers will cover similar incidents. The Binance hack, involving malware in an ad, highlights supply chain risks, while AI’s role in both attacks and systemic risks is noted. Kevin Kalinich warned insurers can handle single large losses but not correlated, aggregated risks from AI errors. Insurers may demand improved security measures and new exclusions in policies.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Three Linux Tools Fix Flatpak's Permission and Storage Issues
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 3 Linux apps that fix Flatpak's most annoying permission and storage problems
Flatpak's sandboxing model causes permission and storage issues, such as restricted file access and leftover data. Three Linux applications address these problems. Flatseal provides a graphical interface to adjust permissions for filesystem access, devices, and sandbox capabilities, allowing users to enable or disable specific resources. Flatpak KCM integrates permission management into KDE System Settings, handling portal-related permissions like location and camera access, and letting users manage remembered settings. Warehouse cleans up Flatpak applications by removing unused data and leftover files from ~/.var/app/, offering features like snapshots and repository management. These tools collectively resolve most Flatpak-related issues, though other utilities like Flatsweep and jdFlatpakSnapshot exist for specific tasks. Terminal commands like flatpak override and uninstall --unused remain useful for occasional maintenance.

item.title: Developer ends screensaver deal with Roku after Fox acquisition
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Developer ends lucrative screensaver deal with Roku because Fox bought it
Developer Jim Sachs ended a 10-year screensaver deal with Roku after Fox acquired the company. The 'Aquatic Life' screensaver, licensed through Prolific Publishing, will no longer be available on Roku devices after December 1. Sachs, creator of the Marine Aquarium animation, cited Fox News' controversial content as a reason to terminate the license. Roku will replace it with the Roku City screensaver, which includes subtle ads. Users expressed disappointment, with one Reddit user calling the screensaver essential for managing ADHD-related stress. Sachs noted the licensing agreement could be canceled by either party, and the deal's termination followed news of Fox's acquisition. The change affects Roku OS users who relied on the ad-free, calming screensaver for years.

item.title: Pentagon approves $250M loan for 6K battery factory
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Pentagon offers battery startup 6K $250M loan to build US factory
The Pentagon has granted conditional approval for a $250 million loan to 6K, a Massachusetts-based battery startup, to construct a factory in Tennessee. The facility will use microwave-powered technology to produce battery materials without relying on Chinese suppliers. 6K previously received a $50 million grant from the Department of Energy under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, but the Trump administration canceled that 2023 award during a review of Biden-era grants, requiring 6K to reapply. The factory’s original 2024 opening date was delayed due to grant cancellation and uncertainties in the EV market. The company’s process heats metals into plasma using microwaves, then deposits them onto surfaces, reducing steps needed to make cathode material—a critical battery component. The technology is said to work across multiple battery types, including lithium iron phosphate (LFP).

item.title: Nvidia Hardware Worth $11.4M Stolen in Oakland-to-Texas Shipment
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished between Oakland and Texas
A shipment of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million disappeared during transport from Oakland to Texas between August 29 and early September. The six pallets were picked up by a food transportation company’s truck and vanished off the grid. Buyers noticed the theft when the shipment was never received. Police traced the truck to multiple stops in San Bernardino County before it disappeared. A grand theft report was filed on September 13, but no arrests or recovery have occurred. Authorities have not disclosed the specific hardware stolen or the method used. The incident is part of a surge in hardware heists, with over $100 million in stolen tech reported since June. Investigators note thieves employ tactics like GPS spoofing and staged police collisions to evade detection. Stolen components are often sold in gray markets or shipped overseas where U.S. tech access is restricted.

item.title: Honor’s New Phone Features Rear Screen for Time and Alerts
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Honor’s Newest Phone Has an Extra Screen—And It’s Not Where You’d Expect
Honor’s new 700 series smartphones include a rear screen on the camera bump, marking the first confirmed built-in display in a specific model. The series features three variants—700S, 700, and 700 Pro—all with the rear screen, which can show time, date, and possibly alerts. Honor’s website hints at additional uses, though product images mainly depict the clock function. The screen could also serve as a selfie viewfinder, though this feature isn’t confirmed. Other details like screen size, resolution, and battery capacity remain unspecified, with preorder availability but no launch date or price listed. Honor’s midrange pricing strategy contrasts with Xiaomi’s premium devices featuring similar rear screens. The phone offers pastel color options, including pink and blue. Honor joins Xiaomi, Vivo, and Acer in adopting rear-display technology, though the feature’s value depends on its cost impact. A graphic showing a cat popping out of the clock adds whimsy to the design.

item.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 lets ChatGPT build interactive tools
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: ChatGPT can now create interactive tools instead of just answering questions
OpenAI's GPT-6 model enables ChatGPT to create interactive tools with graphical elements, buttons, and sliders. Users tested the feature by requesting tools like a room design simulator, ethical dilemma analyzer, life financial planner, solar system visualizer, holiday itinerary builder, and color palette designer. The room design tool allowed users to adjust furniture layouts and color schemes, offering real-time feedback on space efficiency. The ethical dilemma simulator presented scenarios with multiple-choice decisions and analyzed outcomes through ethical frameworks. A life simulator let users tweak income, work hours, and savings to see financial impacts over five years. The solar system tool visualized planetary orbits with adjustable parameters, though accuracy of physics calculations was unverified. Holiday planners provided interactive itineraries with budget tracking, while color palette designers generated hex codes for website redesigns. Users noted the tools' usefulness for experimentation but cautioned against relying on unverified data for major decisions.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Divers Locate WWII Shipwreck Linked to Nazi Spy Mission
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Divers Found a WWII Shipwreck Off Maine Linked to a Nazi Spy Mission
Divers have located the wreck of the SS Cornwallis, a WWII merchant ship sunk twice by German U-boats. The vessel, originally torpedoed near Barbados in 1942, was refloated and later struck again on December 3, 1944, off Maine. After seven years of searching, the Nomad Exploration Team identified the wreck 400 feet below the Atlantic near Mount Desert Rock. The discovery came amid extreme conditions, including freezing water and powerful currents. The sinking was linked to Operation Elster, a Nazi plan to infiltrate the U.S. for intelligence. The Cornwallis, carrying sugar and molasses, was struck by U-1230 just days before German spies were secretly deployed near Hancock, Maine. Of 48 crew members, only five survived. The team used side-scan sonar to scan over 50 square miles of seabed, eventually matching the wreck to historical records. The find aims to provide closure for descendants and highlight a forgotten tragedy. The team plans further exploration using an underwater robot.

item.title: Physicl raises $10M to enhance robot training with realistic simulations
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to develop realistic digital simulations for robot training. Founder Alex de Vigan, previously CEO of Infinite—a company that created 3D product renderings for e-commerce—sees his team’s technology as a solution to robot training challenges. Generative AI’s inability to understand spatial interactions and manipulate objects has hindered progress, prompting Physicl to repurpose its 3D rendering pipeline to create high-fidelity physical models. The startup’s Studio platform offers 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets for synthetic data generation, targeting edge cases like object recognition in clutter. SpAItial, a world model builder, collaborated with Physicl to improve its Echo-3 tool, which generates 3D simulations from 2D images. De Vigan envisions a future where users input vast datasets, like trillions of images or lidar data, to automatically generate high-quality 3D models. SpAItial’s CEO Matthias Niessner called Physicl’s approach revolutionary, enabling on-the-fly data generation for training. Physicl aims to be more than a data provider, offering tools for continuous synthetic data creation.

item.title: China's intelligence agency recruited executive to spy on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Gizmodo Original headline: China's Intelligence Agency Allegedly Recruited AI Executive to Spy on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, to gather intelligence on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The MSS allegedly tasked Huang with persuading Huang to prioritize exporting advanced AI chips to China. Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer, has ties to the AI industry and China Electronics Technology Group, a military vendor. The operation, dating to 2024, coincided with Megaspeed’s expansion, during which Huang was photographed with Jensen Huang. U.S. authorities surveilled Huang for over a year, noting her role in data centers using Nvidia chips for Alibaba. Nvidia’s spokesperson stated the company does not share classified info with customers. Jensen Huang lobbied Trump in 2025 to allow limited GPU exports to China, despite U.S. restrictions. Trump was briefed on the relationship but took no action. Three House committees have requested Huang’s testimony for a November 18 hearing. The report notes Huang failed to secure approval for exporting Nvidia’s Blackwell GPU line to China, highlighting tensions over U.S. export controls and corporate lobbying in the AI chip sector.

item.title: Sony Reintroduces 1979 Walkman Headphones with USB-C
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Sony’s 1979 Walkman headphones are back. (This time with USB-C)
Sony is reintroducing its 1979 Walkman-inspired MDR-3R headphones with modern updates. The original TPS-L2 Walkman, released in 1979, revolutionized portable music playback. The new MDR-3R retains the classic lightweight, open-back design, blue and orange ear pads, and retro packaging. USB-C replaces the traditional headphone jack, with a cable featuring a microphone and remote control. No battery is required, eliminating the need for charging or Bluetooth. Sony preserved the original 23-millimetre driver and adjusted the sound to replicate the 1979 audio experience. A limited-edition Stranger Things variant includes engraved logos and themed packaging. The MDR-3R is priced at $59.99, while the Stranger Things edition costs $79.99. The product launch marks a nostalgic return to the Walkman’s legacy while adapting to modern connectivity standards.

item.title: Call of Duty Composer Explains Multiplayer Music's Unpredictable Nature
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer says multiplayer music requires a 'flexible framework' compared to the campaign with 'dramatic moments' as 'you have no idea how any given match is going to unfold' — 'Multiplayer is completely unpredictable'
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves explained the differences in scoring multiplayer mode versus campaign. He noted that campaign music follows narrative beats and dramatic moments, while multiplayer requires a flexible framework due to its unpredictability. 'Multiplayer is completely unpredictable,' Graves said, adding that music must support the player's experience without hindering gameplay. 'You have no idea how any given match is going to unfold,' he said, emphasizing the need for adaptability. Graves compared multiplayer music to 'the musical equivalent of Master Sergeant Apone in Aliens,' aiming to pump up players with forward momentum and adrenaline. He described multiplayer as having 'a completely different vibe from the campaign,' with music designed to make players feel anything could happen at any moment. The composer highlighted that campaign music aligns with a structured narrative, whereas multiplayer music prioritizes dynamic, player-driven experiences.

item.title: Satellite firms build rockets as launch market struggles
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: You know the launch market is tough when satellite companies start building rockets
AST SpaceMobile, a Texas-based satellite company, announced plans to develop the Blacklift rocket, capable of lifting 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, with commercial launches scheduled for late 2028. CEO Abel Avellan called the rocket 'the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market.' The announcement highlights growing challenges in the launch industry, as satellite operators face difficulties securing launch capacity. Companies are now considering building their own rockets to meet demand. AST is not alone; Cowboy Space also announced plans for a 2028 launch of its Big Iron rocket to deploy orbital data centers. The trends underscore a worsening launch crisis, with investors showing interest in new medium-lift launch market entrants.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: AI Video Generators Turn Text Descriptions Into Short Clips
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: How Do I Make a Video From Text With AI?
AI video generators like Adobe Firefly allow users to create short clips from text descriptions. By inputting scene details, users can generate videos with movement, lighting, and camera effects. The process involves selecting a model, setting parameters like aspect ratio and resolution, and refining prompts for clarity. Clear descriptions, such as specifying camera angles or visual styles, improve results. Adobe Firefly supports free account use with daily generation limits, while paid plans offer more credits. Users can combine generated clips in an editor to build longer videos, adjusting timing and adding text or audio. Commercial use requires attention to licensing, as Firefly uses licensed content and public-domain material. While AI-generated videos can produce atmospheric scenes or product concepts, they may lack realism for precise physical accuracy. Users should review outputs for inconsistencies and ensure reference materials are properly licensed for commercial projects.
